lessons.label: Activity 1

acts.direction: Write a news story of 5 to 7 paragraphs using the structure below. The scrambled information is attached below.
acts.lead:
Instructions: Write a news story of 5 to 7 paragraphs using the structure
below. The scrambled information is attached below.

Scrambled Facts and Information

▪   An announcement was made by the School Principal Dr. Mary Jean
M. Francisquete on Monday that a new program will be implemented
by the school.

▪   The Special Program in Journalism (SPJ) will be implemented by
Badas National High School for School Year 2021-2022.

▪   After the implementation, the school is expected to receive
equipment and facilities related to the resources needed for SPJ.

▪   “We are happy that SPJ will be implemented in Badas NHS because
it will give our children the chance to be better writers and
journalists in the future,” Linda Jesus, one of the parents said.

▪   The aim of implementing the program is to offer journalism
competencies to cater the journalistic skills of students in the school.

▪   Francisquete said that the SPJ implementation became a reality after
parents and other stakeholders wrote a letter to the school to open
the said program.

▪   “We want to give our students the chance to hone their writing skills
and abilities in journalism and also make sure that we can influence
them to love writing,” Francisquete said.

THE LEAD. (Who did what; or What happened? Perhaps When? and Where?
might be in this paragraph.)

2ND PARAGRAPH (In many cases this second paragraph will answer the
questions Why? or How?)

3RD PARAGRAPH (This is where a quote would often appear. This is viewed
by most reporters as essential to keep the story lively.)

4TH PARAGRAPH (Why are you telling me this/what are the implications of
this? (significance))

5TH PARAGRAPH (What will other people think about this? (Moving the
story on, giving it a human context)

6TH PARAGRAPH (How did the event continue? (Important background)

7TH PARAGRAPH (What is going to happen next? (Again, moving the story
on, significance)

acts.direction: Make a news article based on the following facts: Who: National Bureau of Investigation and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas What: They arrested a counterfeiter. They also seized hundreds of fake Philippine peso bills of different denominations. When: The arrest happened last week. Where: It happened in Sta Cruz, Manila. Other details: -- Nestor Mantaring – NBI Officer in charge. -- He presented the counterfeiter in a press conference on Monday afternoon. -- Ronnie Jacobo – the counterfeiter. -- He was a resident of 895 Quezon Boulevard, Sta Cruz, Manila. -- Article 166 is all about forging treasury or bank notes, obligations and securities. -- Jacobo faces charges of violating Article 166. -- Six to twelve years imprisonment – this will be the punishment of Jacobo if proven guilty. -- Marivic Jacobo – Ronnie’s wife. She is an accomplice to the crime. The NBI is also searching for Marivic. -- Regional Director Ruel Lasala – head of the NBI National Capital Region Division. He launched an investigation upon receiving information that the suspect was engaged in the printing and sale of fake 500 and 1,000 peso bills. -- An NBI agent posed as a buyer and bought a fake 500 and 1,000 peso bills from Ronnie and Marivic. -- Wilfredo Villaluz – Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Supervising Agent. According to him, the suspect did a good job. -- Bills were complete with watermark and security thread. -- Upon closer look one would notice that the security thread is actually a sticker. -- The suspect (Jacobo) admitted using CorelDraw and Adobe Photoshop basic graphic design program for his counterfeiting activity. -- The 500 peso bills and the 1,000 peso bills were sold at 75 each. -- 453,000 – the amount of counterfeit bills recovered by the authorities.

acts.lead:
Instructions: Write 3–4 sentences giving your opinion about whether the
school cafeteria should offer more healthy snacks.

●   State your opinion clearly.
●   Give one reason to support your opinion.
●   End with a short, convincing sentence.
Example:
Topic: Is social media helping or harming students today?
I think social media is harming students today. Many students spend
too much time on apps and games, which can make them tired and distracted
from their studies. For example, some students scroll through social media
instead of doing homework. Students should use social media less so it does
not affect their learning.

lessons.label: Activity 5

acts.lead:
Instructions: Write a short editorial (1 paragraph).

●   Start with a strong opinion (agree or disagree).
●   Give two reasons to support your viewpoint.
●   Provide one possible solution (e.g., limit, guidance).
●   End with a closing statement that urges readers to agree with you.
Example:
Social media is both helping and harming students, but I believe it is
mostly harmful. It can help students communicate with friends and learn new
things, but many spend too much time online, which affects their schoolwork
and sleep. For example, students may stay up late watching videos instead of
studying for tests. To reduce these problems, students should set limits on
their social media use and focus on important tasks first. Schools and parents
can also guide students to use social media responsibly. Using social media in
moderation can help students enjoy its benefits without hurting their studies.

lessons.label: Activity 6

acts.lead:
Instructions: Write a well-developed editorial (2 paragraphs).

Paragraph 1:

●   Present your opinion clearly.
●   Explain one positive and one negative effect of social media.
Paragraph 2:
●   State which effect you think is stronger and why.
●   Provide evidence or examples (realistic, simple ones).
●   End with a strong call to action (e.g., encouraging balanced or
responsible use)
Example:
Social media is a powerful tool that can both help and harm students today.
On the positive side, it allows students to connect with classmates, share
ideas, and access educational content online. For example, students can join
study groups or watch tutorials on difficult topics. However, social media can
also distract students, cause stress, and reduce the time they spend on
homework or outdoor activities.
I believe the negative effects are stronger than the positive ones if social media
is not used carefully. Students should be taught to use social media
responsibly and set daily time limits. Parents and teachers can also
encourage activities like reading, sports, or hobbies to balance screen time. By
using social media wisely, students can enjoy its benefits without letting it
harm their health or learning.

acts.lead:
A Day in the Life of ….
Instructions:

items.text: Choose someone to feature: a classmate, teacher, family member, neighbor, or even a school staff member (e.g., librarian, guard, janitor).
Interview the person using at least 5 questions (e.g., daily routine, hobbies, challenges, fun facts).
Write 3-4 paragraphs feature article titled “A Day in the Life of .”
Focus on capturing interesting details, personality, and real experiences.

Add one photo or hand-drawn illustration (optional). Example: Title: A Day in the Life of Mr. Santos, the School Guard Mr. Santos steps through the school gate before the sun has fully risen, his uniform crisp and his flashlight in hand. He smiles warmly as he greets the early students trickling in, locking the gate behind him. “I like being the first one here,” he says. “It gives me time to think and prepare for the day.” Throughout the morning, he patrols the corridors, making sure classrooms are secure and reminding students to put their things away. When someone forgets a book or backpack, he helps them carry it to their classroom. At recess, he watches students play, sometimes pausing to chat he asks about their day, what subjects they like, and even what games they play at home. In the afternoon, Mr. Santos helps guide students out of the school grounds safely. He stands by the gate, waving goodbye, and makes sure no one lags behind. After the last student leaves, he walks around to check every door and window. He says, “My job isn’t just to guard the school — I guard their memories too. I want them to leave knowing they're safe.” As he closes up, his face shows a quiet pride: even in the small moments, he knows he’s made a difference.

acts.lead: Instructions:

items.text: Explore the school campus and identify a “hidden gem”—a place or feature students may overlook (e.g., a quiet reading corner, an art display, a garden spot).
Describe what makes this place special or unique.
Interview at least 1 person who knows something about the location (e.g., librarian, teacher, classmate).
Write a short feature article (2–3 paragraphs) that includes descriptive details, sensory imagery, and interesting facts.

Give the article a catchy title (e.g., “The Secret Garden Behind the Science Lab”). Example: Title: The Secret Garden Behind the Science Lab Paragraph 1 – Description: Tucked behind the science lab, away from the bustling hallways, lies a small garden that most students pass by without noticing. Sunlight filters through the branches of a tall jacaranda tree, casting dappled shadows on the neatly arranged flowerbeds. The air is fragrant with the scent of blooming marigolds and jasmine, and the gentle sound of rustling leaves creates a peaceful atmosphere. A worn wooden bench sits under the tree, inviting anyone to pause and enjoy the quiet. Paragraph 2 – Stories and Facts: Mrs. Alvarez, the school’s biology teacher, explains that the garden was planted by students five years ago as part of a sustainability project. “It started as a simple idea to grow flowers and herbs for the school, but it became a place where students could relax and observe nature,” she says. Over the years, students have added bird feeders, a small pond, and colorful stepping stones. Many report that spending time here helps them focus and feel calm between classes. Paragraph 3 – Reflection / Significance: Though it may seem small and unassuming, this garden is a hidden treasure in the school. It reminds everyone that even in a busy campus, there are spaces to pause, reflect, and connect with nature. For those who take the time to explore it, the garden offers more than beauty—it offers a moment of calm and inspiration in the middle of a hectic school day.

acts.lead:
“River in Crisis: Plastic Waste Threatens Local Fish Population”
San Isidro, Laguna — Residents of Barangay Malinaw were shocked this
week after local scientists released a report revealing dangerously high levels
of plastic waste in the Maliit River, a waterway once known for its clear
water and abundant fish.
According to the team of researchers from Laguna State Environmental
Laboratory, plastic pollution in the river has increased by 63% in the last
five years. The most concerning part of the study shows that if the trend
continues, the community may lose up to 60% of its fish population in the
next five years.
“We found plastic bags, sachets, straws, and even broken toys trapped in
the riverbed,” said Dr. Elisa Ramos, lead scientist of the study. “Fish are
mistaking microplastics for food. Many are getting sick or dying.”
Fisherfolk in the area have also noticed the alarming decline.
Mang Tonyo, a fisherman of 30 years, shared that his usual three kilos of
fish per day has dropped to less than one kilo. “Minsan wala pa nga. Puno
ng basura ang lambat namin,” he said, showing nets tangled with plastic
waste.
Local officials admitted that the river cleanup programs have not been
enough. Barangay Captain Lucia Hernandez urged residents to reduce
single-use plastics and participate in the upcoming community clean-up
next month.
Environmental groups warn that without immediate action, the river may
become biologically dead—unable to support fish or other aquatic life.
“This river feeds families,” Dr. Ramos added. “If we lose it, we lose part of
our community.”

Task:

●    Draw a cartoon showing how the river looks now, full of plastic waste.
●    Include fish, humans, and trash in a visual story:
o   Fish struggling or sick from microplastics.
o   Mang Tonyo trying to catch fish in trash-filled nets.
o   Residents or children holding signs: “Save Maliit River!”

lessons.label: Activity 23

acts.lead:
“Luna and the Sad River”

In the town of Malinaw, there flowed a river that everyone loved. It was
called the Maliit River, and it sparkled under the sun like a long, silver
ribbon. Children played by its shore, fishermen caught fresh fish every
morning, and families enjoyed picnics on weekends.
But one day, Luna, a curious 12-year-old girl, noticed something different.
When she sat by the river, she frowned.
“Why is the water… darker?” she whispered.
Instead of smooth stones and shiny fish, Luna saw plastic bags, sachets,
straws, and even an old broken toy floating in the water.
The fish looked unhappy too. One small fish swam near her, bumping into
bits of plastic.
“Oh no,” Luna said. “Are you okay?”
The fish couldn’t speak, of course, but Luna imagined it saying, “We’re
trying… but the trash is making it hard to breathe.”
That afternoon, Luna went to visit Mang Tonyo, the friendly fisherman who
always told funny stories. She saw him pulling up his fishing net, but
instead of fish, it was full of plastic.
“Mang Tonyo, what happened?” Luna asked.
He sighed. “The river is sick, anak. There’s too much trash. I used to catch
three kilos of fish every day. Now… sometimes I catch none.”
Luna felt a tight squeeze in her chest. How could a river get sick?
The next day at school, Dr. Ramos, a scientist from the community, visited
their class.
“Children,” she said gently, “we studied the Maliit River, and we found that
plastic waste has increased a lot. If nothing changes, we might lose more
than half of the fish in just a few years.”

The whole class gasped.
“But it’s not too late,” Dr. Ramos continued with a hopeful smile. “If we work
together, we can help the river heal.”
Luna’s eyes brightened. She had an idea.
That weekend, with help from her classmates, she organized a River Rescue
Day. They brought gloves, sacks, and posters that said, “A Clean River is a
Happy River!” Even parents and neighbors joined in.
They picked up trash, sorted recyclables, and planted new plants along the
riverbank. It was hard work, but Luna felt proud.
At the end of the day, she sat by the river again. This time, she saw
something wonderful—small fish swimming freely in a cleaner spot.
Luna smiled.
“Don’t worry, little river,” she whispered. “We’re here to help.”
And from that day on, the people of Malinaw promised to take better care of
the Maliit River—so it could sparkle once more and stay alive for future
generations.

Task:

●    Draw a cartoon showing Luna discovering the polluted river.
●    Include:
o   Dark, plastic-filled water
o   Sad or struggling fish
o   Luna’s worried expression

●    Optional: A thought bubble for the fish: “We’re trying… but the trash
is making it hard to breathe.”
